why: Commits 1 to 4 name each link, its policy, the test cases and the ratchet code, and a wrong policy only costs speed, which the prefetch budgets catch. Commit 5 is open-ended: it edits however many admin files the signed-in spec points at, and the executor must trace each fetched address back to the component that draws it and decide when a shared part or a Link handed on as a value is out of scope, across many files at once on the signed-in build the cheap model has to set up itself.
harm_if_wrong: An admin or storefront link loses a prop such as aria-current or scroll, or a screen navigates with a full reload, which the budget tests do not look for, spread over dozens of files.
make_it_cheaper: Run the signed-in spec once while writing the brief and list commit 5's files by path (with the ones to leave out because they pass prefetch or hand Link on), so the last commit is a named, mechanical import swap.
brief_problems: Line numbers in store-layout.tsx, site-parts.tsx, platform-layout.tsx and cart-link.tsx are from 12 November, before steps 0.13, 2.2 and 2.4 edit the same files; the hrefs are the safer anchor and the brief should say to go by them.
e2e/prefetch.spec.ts and e2e/signed-in/prefetch.spec.ts do not exist yet (steps 1.3 and 0.13), so the helper and table shapes commit 3 and 5 edit are unknown to the brief.
The menus e2e case counts requests with 'next-router-prefetch (or an rsc header)': the two do not count the same requests, and the brief should pick one, as e2e/prefetch.spec.ts's helper will.
